glosses: Exempt from paying tax; not subject to taxation.

Of an item being sold with the proprietor paying the taxes on behalf of the consumer, or of an item that exploits a particular loophole (or an intentional temporary waiver of a particular tax by the government.)
exempt from taxation
A jurisdiction that levies low tax rates on certain economic activities, especially to attract wealthy individuals and foreign businesses.
A country-specific calculation of the approximate power delivered by an automobile engine, used to determine a vehicle's road taxation rate. Modern systems may also take emissions into account.
A rate, usually a percentage rate, at which something is taxed.
The reduction of one or more tax rates.
A reduction in the amount of tax that an individual or company has to pay.
Income that is not a wage, such as interest, dividends or realized capital gains from investments, rent from land or property ownership, and any other income that does not derive from work.
A tax levied on the added value that results from the exchange of goods and services.
A withholding; a tax withheld from employees' salaries and paid to the government. The withheld amount is considered a credit in final taxation.
An in-kind tribute in Imperial Russia exacted from the indigenous peoples of Siberia, usually in fur.
Subject to no value-added tax when sold (but in which the supplier can still recover VAT attributable to it).
